Use one row for every editor and reviewer point, including comments you do not accept literally. Preserve the original numbering.

## Decision summary

**Manuscript/version:** [ ]

**Decision and deadline:** [ ]

**Response owner and author approval route:** [ ]

**Files in the authoritative response package:** [ ]

## Blank matrix

| ID | Comment or faithful summary | Underlying concern | Disposition | Response and rationale | Manuscript change/location | Other records affected | Status/verification |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1/R1.1 | [ ] | [scientific/reporting/reader concern] | accept / adapt / investigate / discuss / decline | [ ] | [page/line/section or no change] | [analysis/supplement/abstract/etc.] | open / checked / author-approved |

## Response pattern

For each point:

1. thank or acknowledge without empty repetition;
2. state the concern you understood;
3. explain what you did and why;
4. identify the exact changed location or explain a reasoned non-change; and
5. quote only the short passage needed to make verification easy.

## Completed example

| ID | Comment or faithful summary | Underlying concern | Disposition | Response and rationale | Manuscript change/location | Other records affected | Status/verification |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R2.4 | Dichotomise recovery score for easier interpretation | continuous effect may be hard for applied readers to interpret | adapt | retain continuous primary analysis because an arbitrary split loses information; add predicted-value plot at meaningful reference points and clarify effect size | Results §3.2; Fig 2; Discussion ¶2 | figure script, caption, supplement and abstract checked | author-approved |

**Response text:** “We agree that the practical interpretation required clarification. We retained the prespecified continuous analysis and added predicted values at three clinically meaningful reference points in Figure 2, with corresponding text in Results §3.2. We did not dichotomise the outcome because no validated threshold was prespecified and doing so would discard information.”

## Conflict and new-analysis checks

- [ ] Editor instructions take precedence where they define the decision, but scientific or ethical concerns are raised explicitly.
- [ ] Conflicting reviewer requests are shown rather than silently choosing one.
- [ ] New analyses have a stated purpose and are labelled planned, amended or exploratory accurately.
- [ ] Any protocol, registration, ethics, data, code or authorship implications are addressed.
- [ ] Abstract, tables, figures, supplement and response letter agree.
- [ ] Every author approves the revised manuscript and response.

## Scenario test

Reviewer 1 asks for more causal language; Reviewer 2 says the design is observational. Record the conflict, retain the design-appropriate claim, explain the inferential limit and ask the editor to resolve any remaining presentation requirement. Do not satisfy both by using inconsistent wording in different sections.

## Evidence of done

Retain the decision letter, response matrix, tracked or diffed revision, clean manuscript, regenerated outputs where applicable, verification record and exact author-approved resubmission package.
